# Feed exports — Scrapy 2.14.1 documentation

- Feed exports
- [Edit on GitHub](https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/blob/master/docs/topics/feed-exports.rst)

---

# Feed exports

One of the most frequently required features when implementing scrapers is
being able to store the scraped data properly and, quite often, that means
generating an “export file” with the scraped data (commonly called “export
feed”) to be consumed by other systems.

Scrapy provides this functionality out of the box with the Feed Exports, which
allows you to generate feeds with the scraped items, using multiple
serialization formats and storage backends.

This page provides detailed documentation for all feed export features. If you
are looking for a step-by-step guide, check out [Zyte’s export guides](https://docs.zyte.com/web-scraping/guides/export/index.html#exporting-scraped-data).

## Serialization formats

For serializing the scraped data, the feed exports use the [Item exporters](exporters.html#topics-exporters). These formats are supported out of the box:

- JSON
- JSON lines
- CSV
- XML

But you can also extend the supported format through the
`FEED_EXPORTERS` setting.

### JSON

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `json`
- Exporter used: [`JsonItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.JsonItemExporter)
- See [this warning](exporters.html#json-with-large-data) if you’re using JSON with
large feeds.

### JSON lines

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `jsonlines`
- Exporter used: [`JsonLinesItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter)

### CSV

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `csv`
- Exporter used: [`CsvItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.CsvItemExporter)
- To specify columns to export, their order and their column names, use
`FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS`. Other feed exporters can also use this
option, but it is important for CSV because unlike many other export
formats CSV uses a fixed header.

### XML

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `xml`
- Exporter used: [`XmlItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.XmlItemExporter)

### Pickle

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `pickle`
- Exporter used: [`PickleItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.PickleItemExporter)

### Marshal

- Value for the `format` key in the `FEEDS` setting: `marshal`
- Exporter used: [`MarshalItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.MarshalItemExporter)

## Storages

When using the feed exports you define where to store the feed using one or multiple [URIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier)
(through the `FEEDS` setting). The feed exports supports multiple
storage backend types which are defined by the URI scheme.

The storages backends supported out of the box are:

- Local filesystem
- FTP
- S3 (requires [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3))
- Google Cloud Storage (GCS) (requires [google-cloud-storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/reference/libraries#client-libraries-install-python))
- Standard output

Some storage backends may be unavailable if the required external libraries are
not available. For example, the S3 backend is only available if the [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3)
library is installed.

## Storage URI parameters

The storage URI can also contain parameters that get replaced when the feed is
being created. These parameters are:

- `%(time)s` - gets replaced by a timestamp when the feed is being created
- `%(name)s` - gets replaced by the spider name

Any other named parameter gets replaced by the spider attribute of the same
name. For example, `%(site_id)s` would get replaced by the `spider.site_id`
attribute the moment the feed is being created.

Here are some examples to illustrate:

- Store in FTP using one directory per spider:
  - `ftp://user:password@ftp.example.com/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json`
- Store in S3 using one directory per spider:
  - `s3://mybucket/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json`

[Spider arguments](spiders.html#spiderargs) become spider attributes, hence
they can also be used as storage URI parameters.

## Storage backends

### Local filesystem

The feeds are stored in the local filesystem.

- URI scheme: `file`
- Example URI: `file:///tmp/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: none

Note that for the local filesystem storage (only) you can omit the scheme if
you specify an absolute path like `/tmp/export.csv` (Unix systems only).
Alternatively you can also use a [`pathlib.Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) object.

### FTP

The feeds are stored in a FTP server.

- URI scheme: `ftp`
- Example URI: `ftp://user:pass@ftp.example.com/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: none

FTP supports two different connection modes: [active or passive](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1699163). Scrapy uses the passive connection
mode by default. To use the active connection mode instead, set the
`FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE` setting to `True`.

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

### S3

The feeds are stored on [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/).

- URI scheme: `s3`
- Example URIs:
  - `s3://mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
  - `s3://aws_key:aws_secret@mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3) >= 1.20.0

The AWS credentials can be passed as user/password in the URI, or they can be
passed through the following settings:

- [`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID)
- [`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
- [`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) (only needed for [temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html))

You can also define a custom ACL, custom endpoint, and region name for exported
feeds using these settings:

- `FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL`
- [`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_ENDPOINT_URL)
- [`AWS_REGION_NAME`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_REGION_NAME)

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

### Google Cloud Storage (GCS)

The feeds are stored on [Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/).

- URI scheme: `gs`
- Example URIs:
  - `gs://mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: [google-cloud-storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/reference/libraries#client-libraries-install-python).

For more information about authentication, please refer to [Google Cloud documentation](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication).

You can set a *Project ID* and *Access Control List (ACL)* through the following settings:

- [`FEED_STORAGE_GCS_ACL`](settings.html#std-setting-FEED_STORAGE_GCS_ACL)
- [`GCS_PROJECT_ID`](settings.html#std-setting-GCS_PROJECT_ID)

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

### Standard output

The feeds are written to the standard output of the Scrapy process.

- URI scheme: `stdout`
- Example URI: `stdout:`
- Required external libraries: none

### Delayed file delivery

As indicated above, some of the described storage backends use delayed file
delivery.

These storage backends do not upload items to the feed URI as those items are
scraped. Instead, Scrapy writes items into a temporary local file, and only
once all the file contents have been written (i.e. at the end of the crawl) is
that file uploaded to the feed URI.

If you want item delivery to start earlier when using one of these storage
backends, use `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT` to split the output items
in multiple files, with the specified maximum item count per file. That way, as
soon as a file reaches the maximum item count, that file is delivered to the
feed URI, allowing item delivery to start way before the end of the crawl.

## Item filtering

You can filter items that you want to allow for a particular feed by using the
`item_classes` option in feeds options. Only items of
the specified types will be added to the feed.

The `item_classes` option is implemented by the `ItemFilter`
class, which is the default value of the `item_filter` feed option.

You can create your own custom filtering class by implementing `ItemFilter`’s
method `accepts` and taking `feed_options` as an argument.

For instance:

```
class MyCustomFilter:
    def __init__(self, feed_options):
        self.feed_options = feed_options

    def accepts(self, item):
        if "field1" in item and item["field1"] == "expected_data":
            return True
        return False
```

You can assign your custom filtering class to the `item_filter` option of a feed.
See `FEEDS` for examples.

### ItemFilter

***class*scrapy.extensions.feedexport.ItemFilter(*feed_options: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/library/constants.html#None)*)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/feedexport.html#ItemFilter)**

This will be used by FeedExporter to decide if an item should be allowed
to be exported to a particular feed.

**Parameters:**

**feed_options** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) – feed specific options passed from FeedExporter

**accepts(*item: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/feedexport.html#ItemFilter.accepts)**

Return `True` if item should be exported or `False` otherwise.

**Parameters:**

**item** ([Scrapy items](items.html#topics-items)) – scraped item which user wants to check if is acceptable

**Returns:**

True if accepted, False otherwise

**Return type:**

[bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool)

## Post-Processing

Scrapy provides an option to activate plugins to post-process feeds before they are exported
to feed storages. In addition to using builtin plugins, you
can create your own plugins.

These plugins can be activated through the `postprocessing` option of a feed.
The option must be passed a list of post-processing plugins in the order you want
the feed to be processed. These plugins can be declared either as an import string
or with the imported class of the plugin. Parameters to plugins can be passed
through the feed options. See feed options for examples.

### Built-in Plugins

***class*scrapy.extensions.postprocessing.GzipPlugin(*file: [BinaryIO](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO)*, *feed_options: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/postprocessing.html#GzipPlugin)**

Compresses received data using [gzip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip).

Accepted `feed_options` parameters:

- gzip_compresslevel
- gzip_mtime
- gzip_filename

See [`gzip.GzipFile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/gzip.html#gzip.GzipFile) for more info about parameters.

***class*scrapy.extensions.postprocessing.LZMAPlugin(*file: [BinaryIO](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO)*, *feed_options: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/postprocessing.html#LZMAPlugin)**

Compresses received data using [lzma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lempel–Ziv–Markov_chain_algorithm).

Accepted `feed_options` parameters:

- lzma_format
- lzma_check
- lzma_preset
- lzma_filters

`lzma_filters` cannot be used in pypy version 7.3.1 and older.

See [`lzma.LZMAFile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/lzma.html#lzma.LZMAFile) for more info about parameters.

***class*scrapy.extensions.postprocessing.Bz2Plugin(*file: [BinaryIO](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO)*, *feed_options: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/postprocessing.html#Bz2Plugin)**

Compresses received data using [bz2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bzip2).

Accepted `feed_options` parameters:

- bz2_compresslevel

See [`bz2.BZ2File`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/bz2.html#bz2.BZ2File) for more info about parameters.

### Custom Plugins

Each plugin is a class that must implement the following methods:

**__init__(*self*, *file*, *feed_options*)**

Initialize the plugin.

**Parameters:**

- **file** – file-like object having at least the write, tell and close methods implemented
- **feed_options** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) – feed-specific options

**write(*self*, *data*)**

Process and write data ([`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes) or [`memoryview`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#memoryview)) into the plugin’s target file.
It must return number of bytes written.

**close(*self*)**

Clean up the plugin.

For example, you might want to close a file wrapper that you might have
used to compress data written into the file received in the `__init__`
method.

Do not close the file from the `__init__` method.

To pass a parameter to your plugin, use feed options. You
can then access those parameters from the `__init__` method of your plugin.

## Settings

These are the settings used for configuring the feed exports:

- `FEEDS` (mandatory)
- `FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING`
- `FEED_STORE_EMPTY`
- `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS`
- `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`
- `FEED_STORAGES`
- `FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE`
- `FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL`
- `FEED_EXPORTERS`
- `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`

### FEEDS

Default: `{}`

A dictionary in which every key is a feed URI (or a [`pathlib.Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)
object) and each value is a nested dictionary containing configuration
parameters for the specific feed.

This setting is required for enabling the feed export feature.

See Storage backends for supported URI schemes.

For instance:

```
{
    'items.json': {
        'format': 'json',
        'encoding': 'utf8',
        'store_empty': False,
        'item_classes': [MyItemClass1, 'myproject.items.MyItemClass2'],
        'fields': None,
        'indent': 4,
        'item_export_kwargs': {
           'export_empty_fields': True,
        },
    },
    '/home/user/documents/items.xml': {
        'format': 'xml',
        'fields': ['name', 'price'],
        'item_filter': MyCustomFilter1,
        'encoding': 'latin1',
        'indent': 8,
    },
    pathlib.Path('items.csv.gz'): {
        'format': 'csv',
        'fields': ['price', 'name'],
        'item_filter': 'myproject.filters.MyCustomFilter2',
        'postprocessing': [MyPlugin1, 'scrapy.extensions.postprocessing.GzipPlugin'],
        'gzip_compresslevel': 5,
    },
}
```

The following is a list of the accepted keys and the setting that is used
as a fallback value if that key is not provided for a specific feed definition:

- `format`: the serialization format.

This setting is mandatory, there is no fallback value.
- `batch_item_count`: falls back to
`FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.
- `encoding`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING`.
- `fields`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS`.
- `item_classes`: list of [item classes](items.html#topics-items) to export.

If undefined or empty, all items are exported.
- `item_filter`: a filter class to filter items to export.

`ItemFilter` is used be default.
- `indent`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`.
- `item_export_kwargs`: [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict) with keyword arguments for the corresponding [item exporter class](exporters.html#topics-exporters).
- `overwrite`: whether to overwrite the file if it already exists
(`True`) or append to its content (`False`).

The default value depends on the storage backend:
  - Local filesystem: `False`
  - FTP: `True`

Some FTP servers may not support appending to files (the
`APPE` FTP command).
  - S3: `True` (appending is not supported)
  - Google Cloud Storage (GCS): `True` (appending is not supported)
  - Standard output: `False` (overwriting is not supported)
- `store_empty`: falls back to `FEED_STORE_EMPTY`.
- `uri_params`: falls back to `FEED_URI_PARAMS`.
- `postprocessing`: list of plugins to use for post-processing.

The plugins will be used in the order of the list passed.

### FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING

Default: `"utf-8"` ([fallback](settings.html#default-settings): `None`)

The encoding to be used for the feed.

If set to `None`, it uses UTF-8 for everything except JSON output, which uses
safe numeric encoding (`\uXXXX` sequences) for historic reasons.

Use `"utf-8"` if you want UTF-8 for JSON too.

Changed in version 2.8: The [`startproject`](commands.html#std-command-startproject) command now sets this setting to
`"utf-8"` in the generated `settings.py` file.

### FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS

Default: `None`

Use the `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS` setting to define the fields to export, their
order and their output names. See [`BaseItemExporter.fields_to_export`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.BaseItemExporter.fields_to_export) for more information.

### FEED_EXPORT_INDENT

Default: `0`

Amount of spaces used to indent the output on each level. If `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`
is a non-negative integer, then array elements and object members will be pretty-printed
with that indent level. An indent level of `0` (the default), or negative,
will put each item on a new line. `None` selects the most compact representation.

Currently implemented only by [`JsonItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.JsonItemExporter)
and [`XmlItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.XmlItemExporter), i.e. when you are exporting
to `.json` or `.xml`.

### FEED_STORE_EMPTY

Default: `True`

Whether to export empty feeds (i.e. feeds with no items).
If `False`, and there are no items to export, no new files are created and
existing files are not modified, even if the overwrite feed option is enabled.

### FEED_STORAGES

Default: `{}`

A dict containing additional feed storage backends supported by your project.
The keys are URI schemes and the values are paths to storage classes.

### FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE

Default: `False`

Whether to use the active connection mode when exporting feeds to an FTP server
(`True`) or use the passive connection mode instead (`False`, default).

For information about FTP connection modes, see [What is the difference between
active and passive FTP?](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1699163).

### FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL

Default: `''` (empty string)

A string containing a custom ACL for feeds exported to Amazon S3 by your project.

For a complete list of available values, access the [Canned ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html#canned-acl) section on Amazon S3 docs.

### FEED_STORAGES_BASE

Default:

```
{
    "": "scrapy.extensions.feedexport.FileFeedStorage",
    "file": "scrapy.extensions.feedexport.FileFeedStorage",
    "stdout": "scrapy.extensions.feedexport.StdoutFeedStorage",
    "s3": "scrapy.extensions.feedexport.S3FeedStorage",
    "ftp": "scrapy.extensions.feedexport.FTPFeedStorage",
}
```

A dict containing the built-in feed storage backends supported by Scrapy. You
can disable any of these backends by assigning `None` to their URI scheme in
`FEED_STORAGES`. E.g., to disable the built-in FTP storage backend
(without replacement), place this in your `settings.py`:

```
FEED_STORAGES = {
    "ftp": None,
}
```

### FEED_EXPORTERS

Default: `{}`

A dict containing additional exporters supported by your project. The keys are
serialization formats and the values are paths to [Item exporter](exporters.html#topics-exporters) classes.

### FEED_EXPORTERS_BASE

Default:

```
{
    "json": "scrapy.exporters.JsonItemExporter",
    "jsonlines": "scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter",
    "jsonl": "scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter",
    "jl": "scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter",
    "csv": "scrapy.exporters.CsvItemExporter",
    "xml": "scrapy.exporters.XmlItemExporter",
    "marshal": "scrapy.exporters.MarshalItemExporter",
    "pickle": "scrapy.exporters.PickleItemExporter",
}
```

A dict containing the built-in feed exporters supported by Scrapy. You can
disable any of these exporters by assigning `None` to their serialization
format in `FEED_EXPORTERS`. E.g., to disable the built-in CSV exporter
(without replacement), place this in your `settings.py`:

```
FEED_EXPORTERS = {
    "csv": None,
}
```

### FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT

Default: `0`

If assigned an integer number higher than `0`, Scrapy generates multiple output files
storing up to the specified number of items in each output file.

When generating multiple output files, you must use at least one of the following
placeholders in the feed URI to indicate how the different output file names are
generated:

- `%(batch_time)s` - gets replaced by a timestamp when the feed is being created
(e.g. `2020-03-28T14-45-08.237134`)
- `%(batch_id)d` - gets replaced by the 1-based sequence number of the batch.

Use [printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting) to
alter the number format. For example, to make the batch ID a 5-digit
number by introducing leading zeroes as needed, use `%(batch_id)05d`
(e.g. `3` becomes `00003`, `123` becomes `00123`).

For instance, if your settings include:

```
FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT = 100
```

And your [`crawl`](commands.html#std-command-crawl) command line is:

```
scrapy crawl spidername -o "dirname/%(batch_id)d-filename%(batch_time)s.json"
```

The command line above can generate a directory tree like:

```
->projectname
-->dirname
--->1-filename2020-03-28T14-45-08.237134.json
--->2-filename2020-03-28T14-45-09.148903.json
--->3-filename2020-03-28T14-45-10.046092.json
```

Where the first and second files contain exactly 100 items. The last one contains
100 items or fewer.

### FEED_URI_PARAMS

Default: `None`

A string with the import path of a function to set the parameters to apply with
[printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting) to the
feed URI.

The function signature should be as follows:

**scrapy.extensions.feedexport.uri_params(*params*, *spider*)**

Return a [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict) of key-value pairs to apply to the feed URI using
[printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting).

**Parameters:**

- **params** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) –

default key-value pairs

Specifically:
  - `batch_id`: ID of the file batch. See
`FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.

If `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT` is `0`, `batch_id`
is always `1`.
  - `batch_time`: UTC date and time, in ISO format with `:`
replaced with `-`.

See `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.
  - `time`: `batch_time`, with microseconds set to `0`.
- **spider** ([*scrapy.Spider*](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider)) – source spider of the feed items

The function should return a new dictionary, modifying
the received `params` in-place is deprecated.

For example, to include the [`name`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.name) of the
source spider in the feed URI:

1. Define the following function somewhere in your project:

```
# myproject/utils.py
def uri_params(params, spider):
    return {**params, "spider_name": spider.name}
```
2. Point `FEED_URI_PARAMS` to that function in your settings:

```
# myproject/settings.py
FEED_URI_PARAMS = "myproject.utils.uri_params"
```
3. Use `%(spider_name)s` in your feed URI:

```
scrapy crawl <spider_name> -o "%(spider_name)s.jsonl"
```

For serializing the scraped data, the feed exports use the [Item exporters](exporters.html#topics-exporters). These formats are supported out of the box:

- JSON
- JSON lines
- CSV
- XML

But you can also extend the supported format through the
`FEED_EXPORTERS` setting.

sections.heading: Storages
sections.text:
When using the feed exports you define where to store the feed using one or multiple [URIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier)
(through the `FEEDS` setting). The feed exports supports multiple
storage backend types which are defined by the URI scheme.

The storages backends supported out of the box are:

- Local filesystem
- FTP
- S3 (requires [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3))
- Google Cloud Storage (GCS) (requires [google-cloud-storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/reference/libraries#client-libraries-install-python))
- Standard output

Some storage backends may be unavailable if the required external libraries are
not available. For example, the S3 backend is only available if the [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3)
library is installed.

metadata.section_summary: When using the feed exports you define where to store the feed using one or multiple [URIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier)

sections.heading: Storage URI parameters
sections.text:
The storage URI can also contain parameters that get replaced when the feed is
being created. These parameters are:

- `%(time)s` - gets replaced by a timestamp when the feed is being created
- `%(name)s` - gets replaced by the spider name

Any other named parameter gets replaced by the spider attribute of the same
name. For example, `%(site_id)s` would get replaced by the `spider.site_id`
attribute the moment the feed is being created.

Here are some examples to illustrate:

- Store in FTP using one directory per spider:
  - `ftp://user:password@ftp.example.com/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json`
- Store in S3 using one directory per spider:
  - `s3://mybucket/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json`

[Spider arguments](spiders.html#spiderargs) become spider attributes, hence
they can also be used as storage URI parameters.

sections.heading: Local filesystem
sections.text:
The feeds are stored in the local filesystem.

- URI scheme: `file`
- Example URI: `file:///tmp/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: none

Note that for the local filesystem storage (only) you can omit the scheme if
you specify an absolute path like `/tmp/export.csv` (Unix systems only).
Alternatively you can also use a [`pathlib.Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) object.

metadata.section_summary: The feeds are stored in the local filesystem.

sections.heading: FTP
sections.text:
The feeds are stored in a FTP server.

- URI scheme: `ftp`
- Example URI: `ftp://user:pass@ftp.example.com/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: none

FTP supports two different connection modes: [active or passive](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1699163). Scrapy uses the passive connection
mode by default. To use the active connection mode instead, set the
`FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE` setting to `True`.

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

metadata.section_summary: The feeds are stored in a FTP server.

sections.heading: S3
sections.text:
The feeds are stored on [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/).

- URI scheme: `s3`
- Example URIs:
  - `s3://mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
  - `s3://aws_key:aws_secret@mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3) >= 1.20.0

The AWS credentials can be passed as user/password in the URI, or they can be
passed through the following settings:

- [`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID)
- [`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
- [`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) (only needed for [temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html))

You can also define a custom ACL, custom endpoint, and region name for exported
feeds using these settings:

- `FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL`
- [`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_ENDPOINT_URL)
- [`AWS_REGION_NAME`](settings.html#std-setting-AWS_REGION_NAME)

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

metadata.section_summary: The feeds are stored on [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/).

sections.heading: Google Cloud Storage (GCS)
sections.text:
The feeds are stored on [Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/).

- URI scheme: `gs`
- Example URIs:
  - `gs://mybucket/path/to/export.csv`
- Required external libraries: [google-cloud-storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/reference/libraries#client-libraries-install-python).

For more information about authentication, please refer to [Google Cloud documentation](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication).

You can set a *Project ID* and *Access Control List (ACL)* through the following settings:

- [`FEED_STORAGE_GCS_ACL`](settings.html#std-setting-FEED_STORAGE_GCS_ACL)
- [`GCS_PROJECT_ID`](settings.html#std-setting-GCS_PROJECT_ID)

The default value for the `overwrite` key in the `FEEDS` for this
storage backend is: `True`.

The value `True` in `overwrite` will cause you to lose the
previous version of your data.

This storage backend uses delayed file delivery.

metadata.section_summary: The feeds are stored on [Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/).

sections.heading: Standard output
sections.text:
The feeds are written to the standard output of the Scrapy process.

- URI scheme: `stdout`
- Example URI: `stdout:`
- Required external libraries: none

metadata.section_summary: The feeds are written to the standard output of the Scrapy process.

sections.heading: Delayed file delivery
sections.text:
As indicated above, some of the described storage backends use delayed file
delivery.

These storage backends do not upload items to the feed URI as those items are
scraped. Instead, Scrapy writes items into a temporary local file, and only
once all the file contents have been written (i.e. at the end of the crawl) is
that file uploaded to the feed URI.

If you want item delivery to start earlier when using one of these storage
backends, use `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT` to split the output items
in multiple files, with the specified maximum item count per file. That way, as
soon as a file reaches the maximum item count, that file is delivered to the
feed URI, allowing item delivery to start way before the end of the crawl.

metadata.section_summary: As indicated above, some of the described storage backends use delayed file

sections.heading: Item filtering
sections.text:
You can filter items that you want to allow for a particular feed by using the
`item_classes` option in feeds options. Only items of
the specified types will be added to the feed.

The `item_classes` option is implemented by the `ItemFilter`
class, which is the default value of the `item_filter` feed option.

You can create your own custom filtering class by implementing `ItemFilter`’s
method `accepts` and taking `feed_options` as an argument.

For instance:

```
class MyCustomFilter:
    def __init__(self, feed_options):
        self.feed_options = feed_options

    def accepts(self, item):
        if "field1" in item and item["field1"] == "expected_data":
            return True
        return False
```

You can assign your custom filtering class to the `item_filter` option of a feed.
See `FEEDS` for examples.

sections.heading: Post-Processing
sections.text:
Scrapy provides an option to activate plugins to post-process feeds before they are exported
to feed storages. In addition to using builtin plugins, you
can create your own plugins.

These plugins can be activated through the `postprocessing` option of a feed.
The option must be passed a list of post-processing plugins in the order you want
the feed to be processed. These plugins can be declared either as an import string
or with the imported class of the plugin. Parameters to plugins can be passed
through the feed options. See feed options for examples.

metadata.section_summary: Scrapy provides an option to activate plugins to post-process feeds before they are exported

sections.heading: Custom Plugins
sections.text:
Each plugin is a class that must implement the following methods:

**__init__(*self*, *file*, *feed_options*)**

Initialize the plugin.

**Parameters:**

- **file** – file-like object having at least the write, tell and close methods implemented
- **feed_options** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) – feed-specific options

**write(*self*, *data*)**

Process and write data ([`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes) or [`memoryview`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#memoryview)) into the plugin’s target file.
It must return number of bytes written.

**close(*self*)**

Clean up the plugin.

For example, you might want to close a file wrapper that you might have
used to compress data written into the file received in the `__init__`
method.

Do not close the file from the `__init__` method.

To pass a parameter to your plugin, use feed options. You
can then access those parameters from the `__init__` method of your plugin.

sections.heading: Settings
sections.text:
These are the settings used for configuring the feed exports:

- `FEEDS` (mandatory)
- `FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING`
- `FEED_STORE_EMPTY`
- `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS`
- `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`
- `FEED_STORAGES`
- `FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE`
- `FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL`
- `FEED_EXPORTERS`
- `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`

metadata.section_summary: These are the settings used for configuring the feed exports:

sections.heading: FEEDS
sections.text:
Default: `{}`

A dictionary in which every key is a feed URI (or a [`pathlib.Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)
object) and each value is a nested dictionary containing configuration
parameters for the specific feed.

This setting is required for enabling the feed export feature.

See Storage backends for supported URI schemes.

For instance:

```
{
    'items.json': {
        'format': 'json',
        'encoding': 'utf8',
        'store_empty': False,
        'item_classes': [MyItemClass1, 'myproject.items.MyItemClass2'],
        'fields': None,
        'indent': 4,
        'item_export_kwargs': {
           'export_empty_fields': True,
        },
    },
    '/home/user/documents/items.xml': {
        'format': 'xml',
        'fields': ['name', 'price'],
        'item_filter': MyCustomFilter1,
        'encoding': 'latin1',
        'indent': 8,
    },
    pathlib.Path('items.csv.gz'): {
        'format': 'csv',
        'fields': ['price', 'name'],
        'item_filter': 'myproject.filters.MyCustomFilter2',
        'postprocessing': [MyPlugin1, 'scrapy.extensions.postprocessing.GzipPlugin'],
        'gzip_compresslevel': 5,
    },
}
```

The following is a list of the accepted keys and the setting that is used
as a fallback value if that key is not provided for a specific feed definition:

- `format`: the serialization format.

This setting is mandatory, there is no fallback value.
- `batch_item_count`: falls back to
`FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.
- `encoding`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING`.
- `fields`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS`.
- `item_classes`: list of [item classes](items.html#topics-items) to export.

If undefined or empty, all items are exported.
- `item_filter`: a filter class to filter items to export.

`ItemFilter` is used be default.
- `indent`: falls back to `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`.
- `item_export_kwargs`: [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict) with keyword arguments for the corresponding [item exporter class](exporters.html#topics-exporters).
- `overwrite`: whether to overwrite the file if it already exists
(`True`) or append to its content (`False`).

The default value depends on the storage backend:
  - Local filesystem: `False`
  - FTP: `True`

Some FTP servers may not support appending to files (the
`APPE` FTP command).
  - S3: `True` (appending is not supported)
  - Google Cloud Storage (GCS): `True` (appending is not supported)
  - Standard output: `False` (overwriting is not supported)
- `store_empty`: falls back to `FEED_STORE_EMPTY`.
- `uri_params`: falls back to `FEED_URI_PARAMS`.
- `postprocessing`: list of plugins to use for post-processing.

The plugins will be used in the order of the list passed.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `{}`

sections.heading: FEED_EXPORT_ENCODING
sections.text:
Default: `"utf-8"` ([fallback](settings.html#default-settings): `None`)

The encoding to be used for the feed.

If set to `None`, it uses UTF-8 for everything except JSON output, which uses
safe numeric encoding (`\uXXXX` sequences) for historic reasons.

Use `"utf-8"` if you want UTF-8 for JSON too.

Changed in version 2.8: The [`startproject`](commands.html#std-command-startproject) command now sets this setting to
`"utf-8"` in the generated `settings.py` file.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `"utf-8"` ([fallback](settings.html#default-settings): `None`)

sections.heading: FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS
sections.text:
Default: `None`

Use the `FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS` setting to define the fields to export, their
order and their output names. See [`BaseItemExporter.fields_to_export`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.BaseItemExporter.fields_to_export) for more information.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `None`

sections.heading: FEED_EXPORT_INDENT
sections.text:
Default: `0`

Amount of spaces used to indent the output on each level. If `FEED_EXPORT_INDENT`
is a non-negative integer, then array elements and object members will be pretty-printed
with that indent level. An indent level of `0` (the default), or negative,
will put each item on a new line. `None` selects the most compact representation.

Currently implemented only by [`JsonItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.JsonItemExporter)
and [`XmlItemExporter`](exporters.html#scrapy.exporters.XmlItemExporter), i.e. when you are exporting
to `.json` or `.xml`.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `0`

sections.heading: FEED_STORE_EMPTY
sections.text:
Default: `True`

Whether to export empty feeds (i.e. feeds with no items).
If `False`, and there are no items to export, no new files are created and
existing files are not modified, even if the overwrite feed option is enabled.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `True`

sections.heading: FEED_STORAGES
sections.text:
Default: `{}`

A dict containing additional feed storage backends supported by your project.
The keys are URI schemes and the values are paths to storage classes.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `{}`

sections.heading: FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE
sections.text:
Default: `False`

Whether to use the active connection mode when exporting feeds to an FTP server
(`True`) or use the passive connection mode instead (`False`, default).

For information about FTP connection modes, see [What is the difference between
active and passive FTP?](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1699163).

metadata.section_summary: Default: `False`

sections.heading: FEED_STORAGE_S3_ACL
sections.text:
Default: `''` (empty string)

A string containing a custom ACL for feeds exported to Amazon S3 by your project.

For a complete list of available values, access the [Canned ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html#canned-acl) section on Amazon S3 docs.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `''` (empty string)

```

    "ftp": None,
}
```

A dict containing additional exporters supported by your project. The keys are
serialization formats and the values are paths to [Item exporter](exporters.html#topics-exporters) classes.

sections.text:
Default:

```

    "jsonlines": "scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter",
    "jsonl": "scrapy.exporters.JsonLinesItemExporter",
```

(without replacement), place this in your `settings.py`:

```
FEED_EXPORTERS = {
    "csv": None,
}
```

metadata.section_summary: Default:

sections.heading: FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT
sections.text:
Default: `0`

If assigned an integer number higher than `0`, Scrapy generates multiple output files
storing up to the specified number of items in each output file.

When generating multiple output files, you must use at least one of the following
placeholders in the feed URI to indicate how the different output file names are
generated:

- `%(batch_time)s` - gets replaced by a timestamp when the feed is being created
(e.g. `2020-03-28T14-45-08.237134`)
- `%(batch_id)d` - gets replaced by the 1-based sequence number of the batch.

Use [printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting) to
alter the number format. For example, to make the batch ID a 5-digit
number by introducing leading zeroes as needed, use `%(batch_id)05d`
(e.g. `3` becomes `00003`, `123` becomes `00123`).

For instance, if your settings include:

```
FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT = 100
```

And your [`crawl`](commands.html#std-command-crawl) command line is:

```
scrapy crawl spidername -o "dirname/%(batch_id)d-filename%(batch_time)s.json"
```

The command line above can generate a directory tree like:

```
->projectname
-->dirname
--->1-filename2020-03-28T14-45-08.237134.json
--->2-filename2020-03-28T14-45-09.148903.json
--->3-filename2020-03-28T14-45-10.046092.json
```

Where the first and second files contain exactly 100 items. The last one contains
100 items or fewer.

metadata.section_summary: Default: `0`

sections.heading: FEED_URI_PARAMS
sections.text:
Default: `None`

A string with the import path of a function to set the parameters to apply with
[printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting) to the
feed URI.

The function signature should be as follows:

**scrapy.extensions.feedexport.uri_params(*params*, *spider*)**

Return a [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict) of key-value pairs to apply to the feed URI using
[printf-style string formatting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting).

**Parameters:**

- **params** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) –

default key-value pairs

Specifically:
  - `batch_id`: ID of the file batch. See
`FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.

If `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT` is `0`, `batch_id`
is always `1`.
  - `batch_time`: UTC date and time, in ISO format with `:`
replaced with `-`.

See `FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT`.
  - `time`: `batch_time`, with microseconds set to `0`.
- **spider** ([*scrapy.Spider*](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider)) – source spider of the feed items

The function should return a new dictionary, modifying
the received `params` in-place is deprecated.

For example, to include the [`name`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.name) of the
source spider in the feed URI:

1. Define the following function somewhere in your project:

```
# myproject/utils.py
def uri_params(params, spider):
    return {**params, "spider_name": spider.name}
```
2. Point `FEED_URI_PARAMS` to that function in your settings:

```
# myproject/settings.py
FEED_URI_PARAMS = "myproject.utils.uri_params"
```
3. Use `%(spider_name)s` in your feed URI:

```
scrapy crawl <spider_name> -o "%(spider_name)s.jsonl"
```

skills.description: 根据目标输出格式为 Scrapy 的 FEEDS 设置选择对应的 format 值并配置导出器，覆盖 JSON、JSON lines、CSV、XML、Pickle、Marshal 等内置格式；当需要将抓取到的 item 序列化输出到文件或存储时使用。
skills.skill_body:
为抓取结果选择并配置正确的序列化导出格式：确定目标格式，在 FEEDS 设置中为 format 键填入对应值，确认所用导出器，必要时通过 FEED_EXPORTERS 扩展格式；若为 CSV，使用 FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS 指定列、列顺序与列名。

## Objective

为抓取结果选择并配置正确的序列化导出格式
## Applicable Signals

- 需要将 item 导出为指定格式
- 需要为 CSV 指定列顺序或列名
- 需要从内置格式中选择序列化方式

## Contraindications

- 仅需内存处理无需落盘输出

## Intervention Moves

- 确定目标输出格式
- 在 FEEDS 设置的 format 键填入对应格式值
- 确认该格式对应的导出器
- CSV 场景下使用 FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS 指定列、顺序与列名
- 需要额外格式时通过 FEED_EXPORTERS 扩展

## Workflow Steps

- 确定目标输出格式（json、jsonlines、csv、xml、pickle、marshal 之一）
- 在 FEEDS 设置中为 format 键填入对应值
- 核对所用导出器：json→JsonItemExporter，jsonlines→JsonLinesItemExporter，csv→CsvItemExporter，xml→XmlItemExporter，pickle→PickleItemExporter，marshal→MarshalItemExporter
- 若为 CSV，使用 FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS 指定列、列顺序与列名（CSV 使用固定表头，此项尤为重要）
- 若内置格式不满足需求，通过 FEED_EXPORTERS 设置扩展支持的格式

## Constraints

- format 键取值必须为受支持的格式标识
- CSV 因使用固定表头，列定义应通过 FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS 明确指定

## Cautions

- 使用 JSON 处理大型 feed 时需注意相关警告

## Output Contract

- 已配置 format 键与对应导出器的 FEEDS 设置

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要将 item 导出为 CSV 并指定列顺序
- Therapist/Output: 在 FEEDS 中设置 format 为 csv，并使用 FEED_EXPORT_FIELDS 指定列、列顺序与列名
- Notes: CSV 使用固定表头，列定义尤为重要

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要将 item 导出为 JSON lines
- Therapist/Output: 在 FEEDS 中设置 format 为 jsonlines，对应导出器为 JsonLinesItemExporter

skills.skill_body:
当需要为 feed 导出指定存储位置时，使用 FEEDS 设置配置一个或多个 URI。根据 URI scheme 选择对应存储后端（本地文件系统、FTP、S3、GCS、标准输出）。若需扩展或自定义存储后端，可通过 FEED_STORAGES 相关设置调整。确认每个 URI 的 scheme 与目标后端匹配后再启用导出。

## Objective

为 feed 导出配置正确的存储后端与 URI
## Applicable Signals

- 需要将 feed 写入远程或本地存储
- 需要多目标存储输出
- 需要按 URI scheme 选择存储后端

## Contraindications

- 仅需选择序列化格式而存储位置已确定

## Intervention Moves

- 在 FEEDS 设置中定义一个或多个存储 URI
- 根据 URI scheme 匹配本地文件系统、FTP、S3、GCS 或标准输出后端
- 如需扩展后端，通过 FEED_STORAGES 相关设置配置

## Workflow Steps

- 确定 feed 的目标存储位置（本地、FTP、S3、GCS 或标准输出）
- 在 FEEDS 设置中写入对应的一个或多个 URI
- 确认每个 URI 的 scheme 与目标存储后端匹配
- 如需自定义或扩展后端，调整 FEED_STORAGES 相关设置

## Constraints

- 存储位置必须通过 FEEDS 设置中的 URI 定义
- 存储后端由 URI scheme 决定

## Cautions

- 多目标输出时需确保每个 URI 的 scheme 均正确对应后端

## Output Contract

- 已按 URI scheme 配置好存储后端的 FEEDS 设置

skills.name: Feed 存储后端选择与依赖校验
skills.description: 根据目标输出位置为 Scrapy feed 选择内置存储后端（本地文件系统、FTP、S3、GCS、标准输出），并在使用前校验所需外部库是否已安装，给出可用后端与依赖校验结论。
skills.skill_body:
当需要把抓取结果导出到某个存储位置时，先确定目标位置对应的存储后端，再校验该后端所需的外部库是否已安装；若依赖缺失则说明该后端不可用并给出替代方案。

## Objective

为给定输出目标确定可用的存储后端并确认依赖满足
## Applicable Signals

- 用户指定了输出位置（本地路径、FTP、S3、GCS 或标准输出）
- 用户询问某存储后端是否可用或为何不可用

## Contraindications

- 仅需选择序列化格式而非存储位置
- 未安装所需外部库且无法安装

## Intervention Moves

- 将目标输出位置映射到内置存储后端：本地文件系统、FTP、S3、GCS、标准输出
- 识别该后端所需的外部库（如 S3 需要 boto3，GCS 需要 google-cloud-storage）
- 校验所需外部库是否已安装，未安装则判定该后端不可用
- 在依赖缺失时提示安装依赖或改用其它可用后端

## Workflow Steps

- 确认目标输出位置类型
- 从内置后端列表中选择对应存储后端
- 确定该后端所需的外部库
- 校验外部库是否可用
- 输出选定后端及依赖校验结论，必要时给出替代后端

## Constraints

- 仅使用内置支持的存储后端：本地文件系统、FTP、S3、GCS、标准输出
- S3 后端仅在安装 boto3 后可用
- GCS 后端仅在安装 google-cloud-storage 后可用
- 外部库缺失时不得声称该后端可用

## Cautions

- 部分存储后端在缺少所需外部库时不可用，需在配置前确认

## Output Contract

- 给出选定的存储后端及依赖校验结论（可用/不可用及原因），必要时附替代后端建议。

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 我想把抓取结果导出到 S3，但不确定是否可用。
- Therapist/Output: S3 后端需要安装 boto3 库；若未安装则该后端不可用，请先安装 boto3 或改用本地文件系统等可用后端。
- Notes: 依赖校验结论需明确可用性

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 导出到标准输出需要额外依赖吗？
- Therapist/Output: 标准输出是内置支持的存储后端，无需额外外部库。
- Notes: 内置后端无需外部依赖

skills.name: Feed URI 参数化命名
skills.description: 在创建 feed 时用存储 URI 中的命名占位符（如 %(time)s、%(name)s 及任意 spider 属性）动态生成输出路径或文件名，适用于需要按时间戳、爬虫名或自定义属性区分导出文件的场景。
skills.skill_body:
当需要为 feed 导出生成动态路径或文件名时，检查存储 URI 中的占位符：%(time)s 在 feed 创建时替换为时间戳，%(name)s 替换为爬虫名，其他命名占位符替换为同名 spider 属性（如 %(site_id)s 替换为 spider.site_id）。确认所引用的 spider 属性存在且已初始化，然后生成占位符已被正确替换的最终存储 URI。

## Objective

通过 URI 占位符在 feed 创建时动态替换为时间戳、爬虫名或 spider 属性，生成唯一且可追溯的导出路径。
## Applicable Signals

- 需要按时间戳或爬虫名区分多次导出的文件
- 希望用 spider 自定义属性（如 site_id）命名输出文件

## Contraindications

- 占位符引用的 spider 属性不存在或未初始化
- URI 中需要保留字面量 % 而未做转义

## Intervention Moves

- 在存储 URI 中使用 %(time)s 占位符以在 feed 创建时插入时间戳
- 在存储 URI 中使用 %(name)s 占位符以插入爬虫名
- 使用任意命名占位符引用同名 spider 属性（如 %(site_id)s 对应 spider.site_id）

## Workflow Steps

- 确定导出文件命名所需的动态信息（时间戳、爬虫名或自定义属性）
- 在存储 URI 中写入对应占位符：%(time)s、%(name)s 或 %(属性名)s
- 确认所引用的 spider 属性存在且已初始化
- 在 feed 创建时由占位符替换生成最终存储 URI

## Constraints

- 占位符仅在 feed 创建时被替换
- 非 time/name 的占位符必须对应存在的 spider 属性

## Cautions

- 若引用的 spider 属性不存在或未初始化，占位符无法正确替换
- URI 中需要字面量 % 时应先转义，避免被误当作占位符

## Output Contract

- 生成一个占位符已被正确替换的最终存储 URI。

skills.name: Feed 存储 URI 参数化配置
skills.description: 使用 %(name)s、%(time)s 等占位符及 spider 参数构造 Feed 存储 URI，实现按爬虫或时间分目录存储到 FTP/S3 等后端。
skills.skill_body:
根据目标存储后端与归档维度，构造带动态占位符的 Feed 存储 URI 模板。

执行要点：
1. 确认存储后端（如 FTP、S3）与基础路径。
2. 选择归档维度：按爬虫使用 %(name)s，按时间使用 %(time)s，可组合使用。
3. 将占位符嵌入路径，形成完整 URI 模板，例如 ftp://user:password@host/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json 或 s3://bucket/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json。
4. 若需注入自定义维度，可将 spider 参数作为 spider 属性，并在 URI 中以其名称作为占位符引用。
5. 输出最终 URI 模板，并说明各占位符含义。

## Objective

生成带动态占位符的 Feed 存储 URI，实现按爬虫/时间分目录归档
## Applicable Signals

- 需要按爬虫或时间分目录存储导出文件
- 需要将 spider 参数注入存储路径

## Contraindications

- 目标存储后端不支持 URI 模板占位符
- 仅需单文件固定路径输出

## Intervention Moves

- 确定存储后端与基础路径
- 选择归档维度占位符（%(name)s、%(time)s）
- 将占位符嵌入路径形成 URI 模板
- 将 spider 参数作为属性并以占位符引用

## Workflow Steps

- 确认存储后端（FTP/S3 等）与基础路径
- 选择归档维度：按爬虫用 %(name)s，按时间用 %(time)s
- 组合占位符构造完整 URI 模板
- 如需自定义维度，将 spider 参数作为属性并在 URI 中引用其名称
- 输出 URI 模板并说明占位符含义

## Constraints

- 占位符名称须与 spider 属性名一致
- URI 模板须符合目标存储后端的 URI 格式

## Cautions

- 凭据直接写入 URI 时注意避免泄露
- 确认后端支持所用占位符后再部署

## Output Contract

- 可用的参数化存储 URI 模板，并附各占位符含义说明

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 按爬虫分目录存储到 FTP
- Therapist/Output: ftp://user:password@ftp.example.com/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json
- Notes: 使用 %(name)s 与 %(time)s 实现按爬虫与时间分目录

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 按爬虫分目录存储到 S3
- Therapist/Output: s3://mybucket/scraping/feeds/%(name)s/%(time)s.json
- Notes: S3 后端同样支持 URI 模板占位符

skills.name: Scrapy 本地文件系统 Feed 导出配置
skills.description: 配置 Scrapy feed 导出到本地文件系统，使用 file URI scheme、Unix 绝对路径或 pathlib.Path 对象指定存储目标。
skills.skill_body:
当需要把 Scrapy 抓取结果导出到本机文件时，按以下方式指定本地文件系统作为 feed 存储目标：使用 file URI scheme（如 file:///tmp/export.csv），或在 Unix 系统上省略 scheme 直接给出绝对路径（如 /tmp/export.csv），也可传入 pathlib.Path 对象。确认无需额外外部库。

## Objective

正确指定本地文件系统作为 feed 存储目标
## Applicable Signals

- 需要把抓取结果导出到本机文件
- 用户询问 file URI 或绝对路径写法
- 需要为 feed 指定本地文件系统存储目标

## Contraindications

- 目标是远程存储如 S3/FTP/GCS
- 需要自定义存储后端插件

## Intervention Moves

- 使用 file URI scheme 指定本地路径
- 在 Unix 系统上省略 scheme 直接给出绝对路径
- 传入 pathlib.Path 对象作为存储目标

## Workflow Steps

- 确认导出目标为本机文件系统
- 选择 file URI scheme、绝对路径或 pathlib.Path 之一指定目标
- 确认无需额外外部库即可使用

## Constraints

- 省略 scheme 的绝对路径写法仅在 Unix 系统上可用
- 本地文件系统存储无需额外外部库

## Cautions

- 省略 scheme 的绝对路径写法不适用于非 Unix 系统

## Output Contract

- 可用的本地文件 feed URI 或绝对路径配置

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要把抓取结果导出到本机 /tmp/export.csv
- Therapist/Output: file:///tmp/export.csv
- Notes: 使用 file URI scheme

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 在 Unix 系统上导出到 /tmp/export.csv
- Therapist/Output: /tmp/export.csv
- Notes: 省略 scheme 的绝对路径写法

skills.description: 配置 Scrapy feed 导出到 FTP 服务器，包括 ftp 方案 URI 构造与主动/被动连接模式选择。适用于需要将抓取结果直接写入 FTP 的场景。
skills.skill_body:
当需要将 Scrapy feed 导出到 FTP 服务器时，使用本技能：构造 ftp 方案的 feed URI（形如 ftp://user:pass@host/path/to/export.csv），确认无需额外外部库；默认使用被动连接模式，如需主动模式则将 FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE 设为 True。

## Objective

正确配置 FTP 作为 feed 存储后端并选择连接模式
## Applicable Signals

- 目标存储后端为 FTP 服务器
- 需要指定 FTP 连接模式

## Contraindications

- 目标存储为本地文件系统、S3 或 GCS
- 仅需标准输出

- 使用 ftp 方案构造 feed URI
- 默认采用被动连接模式
- 如需主动模式则设置 FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE 为 True

## Workflow Steps

- 确认目标为 FTP 存储后端
- 构造 ftp:// 方案的 feed URI，包含用户、密码、主机与导出路径
- 确认无需额外外部库
- 默认使用被动连接模式；如需主动模式，将 FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE 设为 True

## Constraints

- URI 必须使用 ftp 方案
- 主动模式需显式设置 FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE

## Cautions

- URI 中包含凭据，注意避免泄露

## Output Contract

- 可用的 FTP feed URI 与 FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE 设置

- Therapist/Output: FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE = True
- Notes: 在设置中启用主动模式

skills.name: S3 导出凭证与 ACL 配置
skills.description: 配置 Scrapy feed 导出到 S3 时的凭证来源（URI 中的 user/password 或 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 设置）以及自定义 ACL、endpoint 和 region。适用于需要将抓取结果写入 S3 存储的场景。
skills.skill_body:
当需要将 Scrapy feed 导出到 S3 时，按以下方式配置凭证与访问控制：
1. 选择凭证来源：可在 S3 URI 中以 user/password 形式传入 AWS 凭证，或通过设置 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID、AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 提供；若使用临时安全凭证，还需设置 AWS_SESSION_TOKEN。
2. 如需自定义访问控制或目标端点，配置自定义 ACL、自定义 endpoint 与 region 名称。
3. 确认导出目标确为 S3；若为本地文件系统、FTP、GCS 或标准输出，则不适用本技能。
4. 输出一份可用的 S3 导出配置，说明凭证来源与 ACL/endpoint/region 设置。

## Objective

正确配置 S3 导出所需的凭证、ACL、endpoint 与 region 参数
## Applicable Signals

- 导出目标为 S3 存储
- 需要临时安全凭证（AWS_SESSION_TOKEN）
- 需要自定义 ACL、endpoint 或 region

## Contraindications

- 导出目标为本地文件系统、FTP、GCS 或标准输出

## Intervention Moves

- 在 URI 中以 user/password 传入 AWS 凭证
- 通过 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID 与 AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 设置凭证
- 使用临时凭证时设置 AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
- 配置自定义 ACL、endpoint 与 region

## Workflow Steps

- 确认导出目标为 S3
- 选择凭证来源：URI user/password 或 AWS 凭证设置
- 如使用临时凭证，补充 AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
- 按需配置自定义 ACL、endpoint 与 region
- 产出可用的 S3 导出配置

## Constraints

- 凭证来源二选一：URI user/password 或 AWS 凭证设置
- AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 仅在临时安全凭证场景需要

## Cautions

- 避免在明文配置中泄露长期凭证，优先使用临时安全凭证

## Output Contract

- 一份可用的 S3 导出配置（凭证来源与 ACL/endpoint/region 设置）

- 导出目标为 S3 或 S3 兼容对象存储

skills.name: Scrapy GCS Feed 导出配置
skills.description: 配置 Scrapy feed 导出到 Google Cloud Storage：使用 gs:// URI 方案，并依赖 google-cloud-storage 库完成认证与写入。当需要把抓取结果写入 GCS 存储桶时使用。
skills.skill_body:
当需要将 Scrapy feed 导出到 Google Cloud Storage 时，按以下步骤执行：
1. 确认目标存储后端为 GCS，导出 URI 使用 gs:// 方案。
2. 按 gs://<bucket>/<path>/<filename> 形式构造导出 URI（例如 gs://mybucket/path/to/export.csv）。
3. 确认已安装并可用 google-cloud-storage 库；若缺失，先安装该依赖。
4. 按 Google Cloud 认证文档配置认证凭据，确保进程具备写入目标存储桶的权限。
5. 将 URI 配置到 feed 导出设置中，并验证导出结果写入目标存储桶。
仅处理 GCS 存储后端配置，不涉及序列化格式选择或其他存储后端。

## Objective

让抓取结果正确写入 GCS 存储桶
## Applicable Signals

- 目标存储为 Google Cloud Storage
- 导出 URI 使用 gs:// 方案
- 需要 google-cloud-storage 库支持

## Contraindications

- 目标存储为本地文件系统、FTP 或 S3
- 未安装 google-cloud-storage 库
- 无法配置 Google Cloud 认证凭据

## Intervention Moves

- 确认使用 gs:// URI 方案
- 构造 gs://<bucket>/<path>/<filename> 形式的导出 URI
- 确认安装 google-cloud-storage 库
- 按 Google Cloud 认证文档配置认证凭据

## Workflow Steps

- 确认目标存储后端为 GCS
- 使用 gs:// 方案构造导出 URI
- 确认 google-cloud-storage 库已安装
- 配置 Google Cloud 认证
- 将 URI 配置到 feed 导出设置并验证写入

## Constraints

- 导出 URI 必须使用 gs:// 方案
- 必须依赖 google-cloud-storage 库
- 认证需遵循 Google Cloud 认证文档

## Cautions

- 认证凭据缺失或权限不足会导致写入失败
- 未安装 google-cloud-storage 库时无法使用 GCS 存储后端

## Output Contract

- 可用的 gs:// 导出 URI 配置及依赖说明（含 google-cloud-storage 库与认证要求）

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要将 feed 导出到名为 mybucket 的 GCS 存储桶的 path/to 目录下，文件名为 export.csv
- Therapist/Output: gs://mybucket/path/to/export.csv
- Notes: 需安装 google-cloud-storage 库并按 Google Cloud 文档配置认证

skills.skill_body:

识别并区分使用延迟文件投递的存储后端

- 需要判断某存储后端是否延迟写入文件
- 导出结果未按预期即时出现需排查存储后端行为

## Contraindications

- 仅使用 stdout 等非文件存储后端

## Intervention Moves

- 确认目标存储后端类型
- 依据延迟文件投递语义判断其写入时机
- 给出是否属于延迟投递类型的结论

## Workflow Steps

- 确认当前 feed 导出所使用的存储后端
- 判断该后端是否采用延迟文件投递语义
- 据此给出存储后端选择建议或排查方向

## Constraints

- 仅作知识性判断，不执行具体配置动作
- 结论需明确所选存储后端是否属于延迟文件投递类型

## Cautions

- 延迟投递可能导致导出结果不即时出现，排查时需先排除该语义因素

- 明确所选存储后端是否属于延迟文件投递类型，并给出相应的选择或排查结论。

skills.name: Feed 压缩导出配置
skills.description: 为 Scrapy feed 导出选择并配置压缩方式（gzip、lzma、bz2），通过 feed_options 传入对应压缩参数，以减小导出文件体积或满足传输要求。
skills.skill_body:
根据目标压缩格式，在 feed 的 feed_options 中设置对应的压缩参数：gzip 使用 gzip_compresslevel、gzip_mtime、gzip_filename；lzma 使用 lzma_format、lzma_check、lzma_preset、lzma_filters；bz2 使用 bz2_compresslevel。仅传入所选格式支持的参数，避免混用不同格式的参数。

## Objective

按所选压缩格式正确设置 feed_options 压缩参数
## Applicable Signals

- 需要压缩导出文件
- 需指定 gzip/lzma/bz2 压缩参数

## Contraindications

- 无需压缩输出
- 目标存储不支持压缩流

## Intervention Moves

- 确定目标压缩格式（gzip、lzma 或 bz2）
- 在 feed_options 中填入该格式支持的压缩参数

## Workflow Steps

- 确认是否需要压缩导出以及目标压缩格式
- 选择对应格式的参数集：gzip（gzip_compresslevel、gzip_mtime、gzip_filename）、lzma（lzma_format、lzma_check、lzma_preset、lzma_filters）、bz2（bz2_compresslevel）

skills.name: 批量 Feed 输出文件命名占位符配置
skills.description: 在 Scrapy feed 导出会生成多个输出文件时，通过在 feed URI 中使用 batch_time 或 batch_id 占位符区分不同输出文件名，并可用 printf 风格格式化控制编号位数。
skills.skill_body:
当一次 feed 导出会生成多个输出文件时，检查 feed URI 是否至少包含一个批次占位符：%(batch_time)s 或 %(batch_id)d。若需要固定位数或可排序编号，使用 printf 风格格式化调整，例如 %(batch_id)05d。确认占位符位于 URI 中会生成不同文件名的位置，然后交付最终 URI 配置。

## Objective

为多文件 feed 输出配置唯一且可排序的文件名
## Applicable Signals

- feed 导出配置将产生多个输出文件
- 需要按批次时间或批次序号区分文件名

## Contraindications

- 仅导出单个输出文件
- 不需要区分批次文件名

## Intervention Moves

- 在 feed URI 中加入 %(batch_time)s 以按创建时间戳区分文件
- 在 feed URI 中加入 %(batch_id)d 以按 1-based 批次序号区分文件
- 使用 printf 风格格式化（如 %(batch_id)05d）控制编号位数

## Workflow Steps

- 确认本次导出会生成多个输出文件。
- 在 feed URI 中至少加入一个批次占位符：%(batch_time)s 或 %(batch_id)d。
- 如需固定位数或可排序编号，改用 printf 风格格式化，例如 %(batch_id)05d。
- 校验 URI 能生成唯一且可排序的文件名后交付配置。

## Constraints

- 多文件导出时 feed URI 必须至少包含一个批次占位符
- 占位符需使用 printf 风格字符串格式化语法

## Cautions

- batch_id 为 1-based 序号，格式化时注意位数与排序需求

## Output Contract

- 包含 batch_time 或 batch_id 占位符的 feed URI 配置

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要按批次序号生成多文件，且编号为 5 位
- Therapist/Output: feed URI 中使用 %(batch_id)05d，使 3 变为 00003、123 变为 00123
- Notes: printf 风格格式化控制编号位数

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要按创建时间区分多个输出文件
- Therapist/Output: feed URI 中使用 %(batch_time)s，替换为创建时的时间戳
- Notes: 时间戳示例形如 2020-03-28T14-45-08.237134

skills.name: Feed URI 参数生成器
skills.description: 实现一个可调用函数，接收默认参数字典与 spider，返回新的参数字典，用于生成 feed 存储 URI 的动态参数（如 batch_id、batch_time、time）。适用于需要按批次或时间动态构造 feed 文件路径、配置 FEED_URI_PARAMS 的场景。
skills.skill_body:
实现一个 URI 参数生成函数：接收 params（默认键值对字典）与 spider（feed 条目的来源 spider），返回一个新的字典，包含 batch_id、batch_time、time 等动态参数。不要就地修改传入的 params（已弃用）。batch_id 为文件批次 ID，当 FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT 为 0 时恒为 1；batch_time 为 UTC 日期时间，ISO 格式且将 ':' 替换为 '-'；time 为 batch_time 且微秒置为 0。

## Objective

为 feed 导出 URI 生成动态参数
## Applicable Signals

- 需要按批次或时间动态构造 feed 文件路径
- 配置 FEED_URI_PARAMS 时

## Contraindications

- 仅需静态固定输出路径时
- 不涉及 feed 导出配置时

## Intervention Moves

- 接收 params 默认键值对字典与 spider
- 构造包含 batch_id、batch_time、time 的新字典
- 返回新字典而非就地修改 params

## Workflow Steps

- 接收 params（默认键值对字典）与 spider（feed 条目来源 spider）
- 生成 batch_id：文件批次 ID，当 FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT 为 0 时恒为 1
- 生成 batch_time：UTC 日期时间，ISO 格式且将 ':' 替换为 '-'
- 生成 time：batch_time 且微秒置为 0
- 返回包含上述键的新字典，不就地修改传入的 params

## Constraints

- 函数应返回新字典
- 就地修改传入的 params 已弃用，应避免

## Cautions

- batch_id 在 FEED_EXPORT_BATCH_ITEM_COUNT 为 0 时恒为 1
- batch_time 使用 UTC 时间且 ISO 格式中 ':' 替换为 '-'
- time 为 batch_time 且微秒置为 0

## Output Contract

- 返回包含 batch_id、batch_time、time 等键的新参数字典

skills.name: Feed URI 动态参数注入
skills.description: 通过定义 uri_params 函数并配置 FEED_URI_PARAMS，将爬虫运行时属性（如 spider.name）动态注入到 feed 导出 URI 中，实现按爬虫或运行上下文区分的动态导出文件名。适用于多个爬虫共用同一导出命令但需区分输出文件，或需要在导出文件名中包含运行时属性的场景。
skills.skill_body:
当需要让 feed 导出 URI 引用运行时爬虫属性时执行本微技能：
1. 在项目中定义一个可导入的 uri_params(params, spider) 函数，返回合并了运行时属性的字典，例如 {**params, "spider_name": spider.name}。
2. 在 settings 中将 FEED_URI_PARAMS 指向该函数的导入路径字符串（如 "myproject.utils.uri_params"）。
3. 在导出 URI 中使用 %(spider_name)s 占位符，例如 scrapy crawl <spider_name> -o "%(spider_name)s.jsonl"。
4. 验证导出时占位符被正确替换为实际爬虫属性值。

## Objective

让 feed 导出 URI 能引用运行时爬虫属性，实现动态文件名
## Applicable Signals

- 导出文件名需要随爬虫或运行上下文变化
- 多个爬虫共用同一导出命令但需区分输出文件

## Contraindications

- 导出路径为固定静态值，无需运行时变量
- 无法在项目中定义可导入的 Python 函数

## Intervention Moves

- 定义 uri_params(params, spider) 函数并合并运行时属性
- 在 settings 中设置 FEED_URI_PARAMS 指向该函数导入路径
- 在导出 URI 中使用 %(spider_name)s 占位符

## Workflow Steps

- 在项目中定义可导入的 uri_params(params, spider) 函数，返回 {**params, "spider_name": spider.name} 等合并字典
- 在 settings 中设置 FEED_URI_PARAMS = "<module.path>.uri_params"
- 在导出 URI 中使用 %(spider_name)s 占位符，如 scrapy crawl <spider_name> -o "%(spider_name)s.jsonl"
- 运行导出并确认占位符被替换为实际爬虫属性值

## Constraints

- uri_params 函数必须可被导入，FEED_URI_PARAMS 使用导入路径字符串
- URI 占位符名称须与函数返回字典中的键一致

## Cautions

- 若函数不可导入或路径错误，占位符将无法解析

## Output Contract

- 配置好的 uri_params 函数与 FEED_URI_PARAMS 设置，导出 URI 中 %(spider_name)s 被正确替换为运行时爬虫属性值

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要在导出文件名中包含爬虫名称
- Therapist/Output: 定义 uri_params 返回 {**params, "spider_name": spider.name}，设置 FEED_URI_PARAMS = "myproject.utils.uri_params"，使用 -o "%(spider_name)s.jsonl"
- Notes: 占位符名称须与函数返回字典键一致
